Radiology Study Report
✛ care
Patient  Jagan
Mobile Number  +91 97777 10000
Age / Sex  26 Y, Male
Doctor  Admin User
Technique
Patient positioned upright facing the detector. PA projection at full inspiration. 120 kVp, 5 mAs, SID 180 cm. No motion artefact.
Findings
Lungs: A 2.4 × 1.8 cm spiculated nodule is identified in the posterior segment of the right lower lobe, demonstrating heterogeneous density. No cavitation. Adjacent pleural tagging noted.

Mediastinum: Mildly enlarged right paratracheal and subcarinal lymph nodes, the largest measuring 14 mm. No pericardial effusion.

Pleura: Trace right pleural effusion. No pneumothorax.

Bones: Degenerative changes of the dorsal spine. No suspicious osseous lesion.
Impression
1. Spiculated 2.4 cm nodule in the right lower lobe with associated ipsilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy — highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy. Tissue diagnosis strongly recommended.
2. Trace right pleural effusion, likely reactive.
3. No evidence of distant metastatic disease within the imaged volume.
